correctness.rationale: A direct population-count reduction exhausts all colour support patterns and all four possible numbers of above-threshold colour classes. EGF counts follow from multinomial allocation; exact sharp cutoffs have constructive witnesses; the singular Gaussian is converted to an ordinary two-dimensional CLT and the critical residue amplitude follows from a local multinomial CLT. A standalone vertex-level implementation checked 280449 finite configurations across all N=3..9 and thresholds 1..N+1 with exact predicted counts and cutoffs. The finite checks are not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2016 general-graph cyclic cellular automaton result assumes contact threshold one and so covers a known special regime, not the positive higher thresholds. The 2021 arbitrary-contact-threshold analysis is on infinite regular trees, not finite complete graphs; the 2025 Boolean network results use two colours and clover majority rules. Neither covers the exact finite state census and lattice-residue coefficient at the critical complete-graph threshold. Targeted literature and published-record searches found no equivalent full statement; priority risk remains for unindexed treatments.
residual_risks: A specialized or unindexed note on the elementary complete-graph threshold model may already contain a subset or all of the finite-state enumeration.
The broader 2016 theorem subsumes some threshold-one conclusions; only the all-threshold combination and associated critical coefficients are assessed as original.
Priority has not been independently certified and searches cannot establish worldwide novelty.

value.rationale: The complete graph is a canonical mean-field benchmark for excitable threshold networks. The theorem gives a complete all-N orbit-and-transient census with sharp existence thresholds, replacing exponentially sized state enumeration. It additionally determines a nontrivial square-root-width coexistence probability and a three-residue 1/N critical amplitude, useful for distinguishing finite-size arithmetic artifacts from genuinely spatial graph effects. Such a natural complete classification meets the value criterion without claiming extension to other graph families.
